source.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry

accepted.question_text: Does every convex body K in R^n admit an ellipsoid E and an absolute constant C such that E captures at least half of its own volume inside K and, after scaling E by a factor C log n, the scaled ellipsoid captures at least half of the volume of K? Equivalently, is there always an ellipsoid E for which vol(E ∩ K) ≥ (1/2) vol(E) and vol(K ∩ C log n E) ≥ (1/2) vol(K)?

evidence.quote:
I Conjecture 5. There exists a constant C such that for any convex body K in R^n, there exists an ellipsoid E that satisfies approximate sandwiching:
vol(E ∩ K) ≥ 1/2 vol(E); vol(K ∩ C log nE) ≥ 1/2 vol(K).

accepted.question_text: If X is drawn from an isotropic logconcave density f on R^n, must the variance of the squared Euclidean norm ||X||^2 be bounded linearly in the dimension? In other words, does there exist an absolute constant C such that Var_f(||X||^2) ≤ C n for every isotropic logconcave density?

evidence.quote: I Conjecture 12 (Thin shell). For X drawn from a logconcave isotropic density f in R^n, Var_f (kXk^2) ≤ Cn

accepted.question_text: For every logconcave density f on R^n with covariance matrix A_f, is the isoperimetric coefficient Φ_f always bounded below by an absolute constant times 1/sqrt(λ_1(A_f)), where λ_1(A_f) is the largest eigenvalue of A_f? That is, does there exist an absolute constant c such that Φ_f ≥ c / sqrt(λ_1(A_f)) for all logconcave densities?

evidence.quote:
I Conjecture 19 (KLS). Let f be a logconcave density in R^n. There is an absolute constant c such that
Φ_f ≥ c / sqrt(λ_1(A_f)).

accepted.question_text: For every isotropic logconcave density f on R^n, is the density at the origin bounded by C^n for some absolute constant C independent of n and f? Equivalently, does there exist an absolute constant C such that f(0) ≤ C^n for every isotropic logconcave density?

evidence.quote: I Conjecture 21 (Slicing). There exists a constant C, such that for an isotropic logconcave density f in R^n, f(0) ≤ C^n.

accepted.question_text: Let f be a logconcave density on R^n, let σ_f^2 denote the largest variance of f along any direction, and let P be any partition of R^n into convex parts. Must there exist an absolute constant C such that the partition-averaged directional variance sum over the parts is always controlled by the global directional variance, namely Σ_P σ_f(P)^2 π_f(P) ≤ C σ_f^2, where σ_f(P)^2 is the largest variance of the restriction of f to the part P?

evidence.quote:
I Conjecture 26. Let f be a logconcave density function and P be any partition of R^n such that each part is convex. Then there exists a constant C such that
Σ_P σ_f(P)^2 π_f(P) ≤ Cσ_f^2
where σ_f^2 is the largest variance of f along any direction and σ_f(P)^2 is the largest variance of f restricted to the set P.

accepted.question_text: Can one design a polynomial-time algorithm that PAC-learns the intersection of two halfspaces in R^n? The paper notes this as a major open problem in the context of learning linear threshold structures and convex concepts.

evidence.quote: It is a major open problem to PAC-learn an intersection of two halfspaces.

accepted.question_text: Is there a strongly polynomial-time algorithm for linear programming, meaning an algorithm whose running time does not depend on numerical accuracy parameters and is polynomial only in the combinatorial size of the linear program?

evidence.quote: In principle, such a dependence can be avoided for linear programming and it is a major open problem to find a strongly polynomial algorithm for solving linear programs.

accepted.question_text: For hit-and-run or the ball walk on a convex body, is there a single deterministic starting point—such as the centroid—that yields the same asymptotic convergence rate as starting from a warm start? More specifically, if one of these walks is started at the centroid, does it mix as fast as when initialized from a random point drawn from a warm-start distribution?

evidence.quote: Open problems. One open problem for both hit-and-run and the ball walk is to find a single starting point that is as good a start as a warm start. E.g., does one of these walks started at the centroid converge at the same rate as starting from a random point?

accepted.question_text: For sampling from a convex body using only a separation oracle, can the reflection walk be analyzed to show substantially better oracle complexity than the ball walk, potentially O*(nD) oracle calls in general and even O*(n) for isotropic bodies?

evidence.quote: It is possible that for this process, the number of oracle calls (not the number of Markov chain steps) is only O*(nD) rather than O*(n^2D^2), and even O*(n) for isotropic bodies. It is a very interesting open problem to analyze the reflection walk.

accepted.question_text: What general classes of distributions or geometric spaces admit efficient random-walk sampling algorithms beyond convex bodies and logconcave densities? In particular, can one give a sufficient condition, formulated using isoperimetry together with a local regularity property of the target density, that guarantees efficient sampling, and for which manifolds with nonnegative curvature can such an efficient sampling process be defined?

evidence.quote: Our next open problem is to understand classes of distributions that can be efficiently sampled by random walks.

Can one provide a sufficient condition that depends on isoperimetry and some local property of the density to be sampled? More concretely, for what manifolds with nonnegative curvature (for which isoperimetry is known) can an efficient sampling process be defined?

accepted.question_text: Can the known geometric condition guaranteeing efficient sampling of lattice points in a convex body be weakened substantially? In particular, can one sample lattice points efficiently from a near-isotropic convex body, or from a convex body that contains at least half of a Euclidean ball of radius O(sqrt(n))?

evidence.quote: Can this condition be improved substantially? E.g., can one sample lattice points of a near-isotropic convex body? Or lattice points of a body that contains at least half of a ball of radius O(√n)?

accepted.question_text: If one is given only random sample points rather than oracle access, can the volume of a polytope with a bounded number of facets be computed efficiently from that sample? The paper poses this as the remaining positive case after noting a superpolynomial lower bound for general convex bodies.

evidence.quote: On the other hand, it remains open to efficiently compute the volume from a random sample for polytopes with a bounded number of facets.

accepted.question_text: Can one learn a polytope in R^n with m facets in time polynomial in m, n, and 1/ε from random examples, either when the samples are drawn uniformly from the polytope or when they are drawn from a Gaussian distribution and labeled by membership in the polytope?

evidence.quote: Thus an interesting open problem is to learn a polytope in R^n with m facets given either uniform random points from it or from a Gaussian. It is conceivable that the complexity is poly(m, n, 1/ε).

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record to the Dagstuhl Publishing page for DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.FSTTCS.2010.42, downloaded the open-access PDF, and mapped the paper structure. Open-question material appears in Section 3 (conjectures) and Section 4 (algorithmic open problems).
Extracted explicit conjectures from Section 3: Conjectures 5, 12, 19, 21, and 26.

Extracted explicit algorithmic open problems from Section 4, including learning intersections of halfspaces, strongly polynomial LP, warm-start replacement, reflection walk analysis, broader efficient-sampling classes, lattice-point sampling, volume from random samples, and polytope learning from samples.

Kept distinct conjectures and open problems separate. Did not merge the volume-from-random-samples question with the learn-a-polytope question because the paper states them as different tasks even though one might imply the other.
Accepted only items with explicit open-problem language or explicit conjecture statements visible in the paper. Rewrites expand notation and context without adding unsupported facts.
